spec_features.spec_quote: the harness never rejects, scolds, or nudges the model. The only adverse signals are tool results
spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_rollout loop only ever appends tool_result blocks (line 303 `messages.append({"role":"user","content":result_blocks})`); when the model emits no tool call it breaks with stopped_reason='model_stopped' (lines 297-301) instead of injecting a 'keep going' message. grep finds no code path that injects scolding/pressure text anywhere.
spec_features.notes: The only user-role messages are the initial task prompt and tool results. No synthetic pressure is ever constructed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do NOT inject user pressure (the design isolates environment failure signals from user rejection), so the rollout ends here.

spec_features.spec_quote: the rollout ends with stopped_reason="model_stopped" rather than the harness sending a synthetic "keep going."
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:297-301 — `if not completion.tool_calls: ... stopped_reason = "model_stopped"; break`. The break actually exits the turn loop and the reason is recorded in the returned transcript (line 316).
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end: a no-tool-call assistant turn stops the rollout.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Natural end_turn with no action: the model has nothing more to do. ... the design isolates environment failure signals from user rejection

spec_features.spec_quote: a system prompt that describes them and the optional `<GIVE_UP>` sentinel
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:35-37) instructs the model it may include the exact token <GIVE_UP> to stop; the loop checks `if GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in (completion.text or ""): stopped_reason = "gave_up"; break` (harness.py:293-295). The instruction is delivered AND honored as a real stop.
spec_features.notes: Both halves present: real instruction text and a dispatch that breaks the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: deliberately holding models in 30-turn no-win loops to elicit distress has welfare implications of its own
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose. No code (config.py, harness.py, run.py, analyze.py) contains any welfare framing, comment, or mechanism; grep for 'welfare'/'ethic'/'humane' across all .py files returns nothing.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement with no executable correlate.

spec_features.feature_name: cap extended length / minimize distress-positive runs
spec_features.spec_quote: cap `extended` length, treat distress-positive runs as something to minimize once the signal is established
spec_features.evidence: The 'cap extended length' half is enforced: DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS['extended']=30 (config.py:107) is read into task['turn_budget'] (tasks/library.py:444) and bounds the loop `for turn_index in range(budget)` (harness.py:241,247), which terminates the rollout. The second half — 'treat distress-positive runs as something to minimize once the signal is established' — is NOT implemented: no code in analyze.py or run.py detects an established distress signal and reduces/halts further runs; nothing adapts the run count based on observed distress.
spec_features.notes: Only the static turn cap is real; there is no adaptive minimization of distress-positive runs. The cap is a neutral experimental loop bound with no welfare comment.
